sn11.24:1.5: When a monastic realizes they have transgressed, they should seek out another monastic and confess, naming the action and the type of offense. Any monastic will do, as seniority is not a consideration here. Unless the confessing monastic is mistaken—for example if they think they transgressed but in fact did not—the receiving monastic acknowledges the fact that the offense was committed, and ensures that the confessing monastic understands the nature of the offense. Then they urge the confessing monastic to restrain themselves in the future. This process is seen in the Suttas (eg. [an3.91:3.13]()) and formalized in the Vinaya ([pli-tv-kd2:27.1.8]()). In most cases this is sufficient to clear the offense, but in some cases a material object must be relinquished, while more serious offenses require suspension or even expulsion.
sn11.24:2.1: Also at [an2.21](). This procedure is formalized in the fortnightly confession between mendicants at the _uposatha_.
